newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Bow Valley unfazed by sanctions concerns.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Bow Valley unfazed by sanctions concerns.

text.p: Canada's Bow Valley Energy, which has just signed a multi-million-dollar deal to develop an Iranian offshore oil field, will go ahead with the project regardless of any threat of sanctions by the United States, the company's president said on Tuesday.

"Bow Valley's a Canadian company and we have no desire to become involved in the political affairs or the policies of the United States," Bow Valley President Walt DeBoni told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Bow Valley, whose chairman is Canadian oilman Daryl (Doc) Seaman, last week signed a deal with the government of Iran to develop the Balal field over a three to four year period under a service contract.
The cost of developing the field, which has recoverable oil reserves of 117 million barrels, would be between $152 and $212 million, DeBoni said.

The deal runs the risk of falling foul of the United States' Iran Libya Sanctions Act, which allows the U.S. administration to penalize foreign firms that invest more than $40 million a year in the two states' oil and gas sector.
U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato, an architect of the act, warned Bow Valley in June not to go ahead with the project.

"We understand what the U.S. is trying to do," BeBoni said. "We don't agree with their approach and our government is strongly on the record as opposing extraterritorial measures such as the Iran Libya Sanctions Act. We certainly live by the laws of our country."
He said U.S. officials had not been in contact with Bow Valley in the days following the signing of the Balal deal.
The field, which has a capacity of 40,000 barrels a day, was discovered in the late 1960s.
DeBoni said development would involve construction of two drilling platforms and one processing platform.
The oil would be pipelined to shore at Lavan Island, where there are more processing as well as export facilities.
Under the service contract terms, Bow Valley will provide financing and technical knowhow to build the project's various parts and be repaid its capital plus a bonus for completion, he said.

Bow Valley, currently a private firm, carries the same name as that of the company started by Doc and his brother B.J. Seaman decades ago. Bow Valley Industries, later Bow Valley Energy, grew into an international oil company with operations in Canada, the North Sea and Indonesia.
It was acquired by Talisman Energy Inc in 1994 for C$1.8 billion.
DeBoni said the new Bow Valley had plans to go public "in the very near future, adding that he hoped the Balal deal would "in a small way...build a bridge between the West and the Middle East.
"There's opportunities for a significant improvement in relations here and I think everyone should take notice of that," DeBoni said. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
